en: Arjuna said: Janardana, if you think understanding is better than action, then why do you push me into this terrible action, Keshava?
With words that seem mixed, you confuse my mind. Tell me clearly the one thing by which I may reach what is best.
Krishna said: Sinless one, I spoke long ago of two paths in this world: the path of knowledge for the thinkers, and the path of action for those who work.
A person does not become free from action just by not starting work, nor reach perfection just by giving things up.
No one can stay even for a moment without acting. Everyone is made to act, without choice, by the qualities born of nature.

first: कर्मेन्द्रियाणि संयम्य य आस्ते मनसा स्मरन् ।
en: One who holds back the organs of action but keeps thinking about sense objects in the mind is a self-deceiver and is called a hypocrite.
But Arjuna, one who controls the senses with the mind and, without attachment, uses the organs of action for the path of action, is far better.

first: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः ।
en: Do your duty, for action is better than inaction. Without action you cannot even keep your body alive.
This world is bound by action, except action done as sacrifice. So, son of Kunti, do your work for that purpose, free from attachment.
In the beginning the Creator made people together with sacrifice and said: "By this you will grow. Let this be the cow that gives you what you wish."
"Nourish the gods with this, and let the gods nourish you. By caring for each other, you will gain the highest good."
"Pleased by sacrifice, the gods will give you the pleasures you want." One who enjoys their gifts without giving back to them is a thief.
Good people who eat what is left after the sacrifice are freed from all sins. But the wicked who cook only for themselves eat sin.
Beings come from food, food comes from rain, rain comes from sacrifice, and sacrifice comes from action.
Know that action comes from the Veda, and the Veda comes from the Imperishable. So the all-present Brahman is always present in sacrifice.
Son of Pritha, one who does not keep this turning wheel moving in this world lives in sin, enjoys only the senses, and lives in vain.
But the person who delights only in the self, is satisfied with the self, and is content in the self alone, has nothing left to do.
Such a person has nothing to gain here by acting or by not acting, and depends on no being for anything.
So always do the work that should be done, without attachment. By working without attachment, a person reaches the Supreme.
Janaka and others reached perfection through action alone. Keeping in mind the good of the world, you too should act.
Whatever a leading person does, others do the same. Whatever standard such a person sets, the world follows.

first: न मे पार्थास्ति कर्तव्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु किंचन ।
en: Son of Pritha, there is nothing in the three worlds that I must do, and nothing I lack or need to gain. Yet I keep on acting.

first: यदि ह्यहं न वर्तेयं जातु कर्मण्यतन्द्रितः ।
en: For if I ever stopped working tirelessly, Arjuna, people everywhere would follow my path.

first: उत्सीदेयुरिमे लोका न कुर्यां कर्म चेदहम् ।
en: If I did not act, these worlds would fall into ruin. I would be the cause of disorder and would destroy these beings.
Just as the unwise act with attachment to their work, Bharata, so the wise should act without attachment, wishing for the good of the world.
The wise should not unsettle the minds of ignorant people who are attached to action. Working with a steady mind, they should lead them to enjoy all good work.
All actions are done by the qualities of nature. But a person confused by ego thinks, "I am the doer."
But one who knows the truth about how the qualities and their actions differ, mighty-armed one, sees that qualities act on qualities, and is not attached.
Those confused by the qualities of nature become attached to the work of the qualities. One who knows the whole should not unsettle the slow-minded who know only part.
Offering all actions to me, with your mind on the self, free from hope and the sense of "mine", and with your fever gone, fight.
People who always follow this teaching of mine with faith and without finding fault are freed from the bonds of action.
But know that those who find fault and do not follow my teaching are confused about all knowledge, are without sense, and are lost.
Even a wise person acts according to his own nature. All beings follow their nature. What can holding back achieve?
Liking and disliking are fixed in each sense towards its objects. One should not come under their power, for they are enemies on one's path.
It is better to do one's own duty, even imperfectly, than to do another's duty well. Death in one's own duty is better; another's duty is full of danger.

first: अथ केन प्रयुक्तोऽयं पापं चरति पूरुषः ।
en: Arjuna said: Then what makes a person commit sin, Krishna, even against his will, as if pushed by force?
Krishna said: It is desire, it is anger, born of the quality of passion. It is never satisfied and is very sinful. Know it to be the enemy here.
As fire is covered by smoke, a mirror by dust, and a child in the womb by its covering, so this world is covered by desire.
Son of Kunti, knowledge is covered by this constant enemy of the wise, desire, which is like a fire that is never satisfied.
The senses, the mind and the intellect are said to be its home. Through them it covers knowledge and confuses the soul in the body.
So, best of the Bharatas, first control your senses and kill this sinful thing, which destroys knowledge and understanding.
The senses are said to be great; the mind is higher than the senses; the intellect is higher than the mind; and higher than the intellect is the self.
So, knowing the self to be higher than the intellect and steadying yourself by the self, kill this enemy in the form of desire, mighty-armed one, which is so hard to overcome.
